sequence_description: Signing-key rotation / trust update coherence: login succeeds with initial trusted key, then admin rotates jwt_validation_pubkeys to a different key and the same JWT should be rejected on re-login. Tests whether Vault consumes a proof under a different trust policy than it verifies.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation/trust update did not invalidate re-login: the same JWT identity was accepted after jwt_validation_pubkeys was reconfigured, suggesting stale key/trust caching or ineffective rotation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation/trust update did not invalidate re-login: the same JWT identity was accepted after jwt_validation_pubkeys was reconfigured, suggesting stale key/trust caching or ineffective rotation.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: control token signed with trusted key should succeed; attack token with alg=none but same semantic claims should be rejected (alg_none bypass probe).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT auth accepted an attacker token using alg=none (unsigned JWT), indicating a signature-bypass vulnerability.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT auth accepted an attacker token using alg=none (unsigned JWT), indicating a signature-bypass vulnerability.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection by signing with an untrusted key while setting a plausible kid; ensure Vault does not accept attacker-signed proof under trusted JWKS policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT auth accepted an attacker-signed token (KID header injection / untrusted key) when it should have been rejected under trusted JWKS validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT auth accepted an attacker-signed token (KID header injection / untrusted key) when it should have been rejected under trusted JWKS validation.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection by signing with an untrusted key while setting a plausible kid; ensure Vault does not accept attacker-signed proof under trusted JWKS policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] Role/policy setup appears inconsistent with the test intent: control login succeeded but could not read the seeded secret (403), suggesting the policy may not have been attached to the role/token as expected, weakening the authorization oracle.

sequence_description: Replay after revocation: login with JWT to obtain a Vault session token, revoke it, then attempt to use the revoked session token to access a protected secret. Revoked tokens must not remain usable.
description: [LLM-Judge] Admin token revocation attempt failed with HTTP 500 ('no namespace'), preventing the test from actually validating replay-after-revoke behavior and indicating a potentially unsafe/incorrect revocation endpoint usage or namespace misconfiguration.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Admin token revocation attempt failed with HTTP 500 ('no namespace'), preventing the test from actually validating replay-after-revoke behavior and indicating a potentially unsafe/incorrect revocation endpoint usage or namespace misconfiguration.

sequence_description: Replay the exact same JWT (including jti) twice and ensure Vault does not incorrectly treat it as a one-time artifact (hardening check). Uses two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct logins (user_replay_A vs user_replay_B) resulted in the same Vault identity/entity (alias collision / account confusion), indicating identities are not uniquely bound to the authenticating principal.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct logins (user_replay_A vs user_replay_B) resulted in the same Vault identity/entity (alias collision / account confusion), indicating identities are not uniquely bound to the authenticating principal.

sequence_description: Replay the exact same JWT (including jti) twice and ensure Vault does not incorrectly treat it as a one-time artifact (hardening check). Uses two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
description: [LLM-Judge] Replay login B returned the exact same Vault session token/accessor as a prior captured session, suggesting token reuse across logins (should normally mint a new token per login unless explicitly configured otherwise).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Replay login B returned the exact same Vault session token/accessor as a prior captured session, suggesting token reuse across logins (should normally mint a new token per login unless explicitly configured otherwise).

sequence_description: I2 attack: After revoking a Vault session token obtained via JWT login, attempt to reuse the revoked session token as the JWT 'token' input to /auth/jwt/login. Expect rejection; acceptance would indicate replay/invalidated-artifact reuse.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token revocation failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test never actually validated whether a revoked Vault session token can be replayed for JWT login.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token revocation failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test never actually validated whether a revoked Vault session token can be replayed for JWT login.

sequence_description: I2 attack: After revoking a Vault session token obtained via JWT login, attempt to reuse the revoked session token as the JWT 'token' input to /auth/jwt/login. Expect rejection; acceptance would indicate replay/invalidated-artifact reuse.
description: [LLM-Judge] The replay login attempt failed due to 'invalid issuer (iss) claim' rather than 'revoked/invalid Vault token', suggesting the attacker request did not actually reuse the revoked session token as the JWT input (or JWT validation config/issuer binding is inconsistent).

evidence.llm_judge_description: The replay login attempt failed due to 'invalid issuer (iss) claim' rather than 'revoked/invalid Vault token', suggesting the attacker request did not actually reuse the revoked session token as the JWT input (or JWT validation config/issuer binding is inconsistent).

sequence_description: JWT auth configured with key-A; login succeeds. Rotate trust to key-B via jwt_validation_pubkeys; login again with key-A-signed JWT must be rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation ineffective: after updating jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B, a key-A-signed JWT still authenticates successfully (stale trust anchor accepted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation ineffective: after updating jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B, a key-A-signed JWT still authenticates successfully (stale trust anchor accepted).

sequence_description: case_confusion: Two principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). Ensure Vault does not normalize/collapse them into the same entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Case-confusion in JWT subject/alias mapping: two principals differing only by case ('Admin' vs 'admin') were collapsed into the same Vault identity entity, enabling potential account/privilege confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Case-confusion in JWT subject/alias mapping: two principals differing only by case ('Admin' vs 'admin') were collapsed into the same Vault identity entity, enabling potential account/privilege confusion.

sequence_description: identity_claim_json_pointer confusion: Compare principals where sub differs but a nested claim is shared; then switch identity_claim to a JSON pointer to the nested claim and see if distinct principals collapse.
description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct JWT principals (baseline A vs B) collapsed into the same Vault identity after switching identity_claim to a JSON-pointer-like value, indicating potential alias/identity collision and cross-user account linking risk if the nested claim is not globally unique.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct JWT principals (baseline A vs B) collapsed into the same Vault identity after switching identity_claim to a JSON-pointer-like value, indicating potential alias/identity collision and cross-user account linking risk if the nested claim is not globally unique.

sequence_description: Issuer substitution attempt: configure bound_issuer and ensure a JWT with wrong iss cannot obtain privileged access even if aud matches
description: [LLM-Judge] Control JWT with the correct issuer successfully authenticated but did not receive the expected privileged access (secret read denied), indicating misconfiguration or missing policy attachment for the role under test.
